values.goal: Understand the scene graph, model loading, and GPU resource lifetimes, and build a measurable 3D inspector.
values.capstone: A 3D inspector with model selection, camera fitting, animation, minimap, and error recovery, plus a resource and performance report

values.concepts.0.title: GLB loading state and recovery
values.concepts.0.explanation: Remove the old model only after the replacement parses successfully. Failed requests preserve it. A request number rejects stale successful results and releases their real resources. This unit observes success/error recovery; unit 24 studies reversed completion order.
values.concepts.1.title: Select model descendants
values.concepts.1.explanation: recursive=true tests descendants. Reading the canvas rectangle on every click preserves coordinates after resize. Replacing the file rebuilds the list for the current model and clears the old highlight.
values.outcomes.0: Keep the UI usable after failure and highlight only the selected object.
values.outcomes.1: Leave other objects with a shared material unchanged.
values.steps.0:
Import GLTFLoader from the same 0.186.1 installation as core. loader.parseAsync(buffer, "") reads an ArrayBuffer and resolves a Promise with scene and animations. status remains loading until await completes, then becomes ready or error. Loading and error text are HTML elements, readable even without WebGL objects.

This starter intentionally reads corrupt bytes, so re-running repeats the failure. Select static and click Load sample. Alternatively change the final sample('invalid') to sample('static') in the editor and run. Load textured to see the embedded 2×2 PNG on both panels. Try corrupt GLB again and confirm that the old model and HTML controls survive.

File input uses file.arrayBuffer(). Only self-contained GLB up to 2 MiB is accepted; external URIs and Draco/Meshopt/KTX2 are rejected before parsing. Multi-file .gltf is unsupported. Selected files exist only during this run and are excluded from backups. Reselect after re-run, reload, or restore. Restoring code/notes does not restore the selected file.
values.steps.1:
A GLB scene is a parent containing meshes. Passing only [root] with recursive=false misses its children because the parent has no triangles. Change recursive to true and click the left panel. NDC uses the current canvas rectangle; hits[0] is the nearest intersection.

Also select Left and Right from the object list. Both the list and ray call the same highlight function. Click empty space or Clear selection to restore color. Repeat with textured and after a file failure. The list displays names, while selection uses actual object references from the current meshes array.
values.steps.2:
Both static panels reference the same mesh and material indices in GLB. Check shared at load=true and material identity. With isolateMaterial=false, changing one shared color turns both panels orange.

Set isolateMaterial to true. Selection clones original material and assigns it only to the selected mesh. Before switching to Right, restore Left's original material and dispose the highlight clone. Clearing selection should restore blue and shared identity. In textured, original and clone still share map references, so clearing a highlight must not dispose the map.

values.concepts.0.title: World center and size
values.concepts.0.explanation: Use the world center for controls.target and camera position instead of moving the model. Placing the camera along +Z from that center gives a front view of this static scene. Model coordinates remain unchanged.
values.concepts.1.title: Fit camera from FOV and aspect
values.concepts.1.explanation: FOV is in degrees while Math.sin takes radians. Using vertical FOV alone can clip sides in a portrait view. Sphere fitting is conservative rather than optimal for each shape, but contains this bound from every direction.
values.outcomes.0: Center a model on screen even when it is far from the origin.
values.outcomes.1: Preserve the camera for an empty model and distinguish small models from empty bounds.
values.steps.0:
offset is a GLB with both panels scaled by 8 and centered at (40,-15,3). values.steps.0:

Read names and duration from the loader result animations array. new THREE.AnimationMixer(root) targets this model; mixer.clipAction(clips[0]) returns an action, and action.play() schedules it for evaluation. animated has SlideLeft with duration=1 second. Repeat static → animated → static and check that previous playback does not remain active.
values.steps.1:
Animation timestamps use milliseconds; AnimationMixer.update(delta) expects seconds. seconds=false passes now-last directly and advances mixer time 1000× too fast. Set seconds=true and read actual delta such as .016s together with mixer time. A 60Hz rate is not guaranteed, so do not hard-code delta=.016.

Play after pause resets last=0 so waiting time is not added in one step. Compare mixer.time growth over about one real second. Left loops from X=-1.1 to -.1, so X alone cannot reveal total elapsed time. Compare at speed 1, then use 2 and check roughly twice the mixer-time growth over equal wall time.
values.steps.2:
The starter prepares an action but playing=false leaves time unchanged. Click Play and read X and mixer time. Pause preserves the pose using action.paused=true; Play resumes from it. Stop and rewind uses action.stop(), reset(), and mixer.time=0 to restore the start pose.

Enter speed=2 and Apply speed. mixer.timeScale=2 evaluates twice as fast over equal real time. Speed 0 is valid and leaves UI live. Compare stop → play, loading clipless static, and loading animated again. Cleanup separately stops the loop, calls stopAllAction()/uncacheRoot(root), and releases actual model resources.

values.concepts.0.explanation: opacity alone does not move a material into the transparent pass. Set needsUpdate after changing transparent. MeshBasicMaterial removes lighting differences from this comparison.
values.concepts.1.title: Compare depthWrite
values.concepts.1.explanation: Transparent objects generally blend back to front, often benefiting from disabled depth writes. Intersecting surfaces have no single front/back object order, so this setting cannot fully solve them.
values.outcomes.0: Distinguish opaque depth handling from transparent compositing.
values.outcomes.1: Explain remaining sorting limitations with screenshots.
values.steps.0:
The starter has opacity=.45 but transparent=false, so the planes render opaque. Enable transparent and Apply. opacity=.45 controls the source contribution; blending must be enabled to mix with colors behind it. Compare 0, .45, and 1 at the same overlap.

red rotates Y=.65rad and blue Y=-.65rad; DoubleSide shows their back faces too. Change one input, Apply, and read actual material values alongside the image. Even opacity=0 can write depth with depthWrite=true and hide later surfaces; distinguish that in the next step.
values.steps.1:
Keep transparent=true and opacity=.45. The starter has depthWrite=true. With intersecting planes, depth already written by part of one plane can block later blending. Disable only depthWrite, Apply, and compare left/right overlaps at the same view.

depthTest stays true. depthWrite=false stops writing this surface depth; it does not disable testing against previously drawn opaque objects. Compare on/off under auto and red-last separately. Reducing missing surfaces does not guarantee correct blending order.
values.steps.2:
With transparent=true and depthWrite=false, apply auto → red-last → blue-last separately. renderOrder=1 draws an object later within this transparent list. Equal-depth centers still force auto sorting to put one whole object first.

At the same front view, changing order changes overlap color. Drawing red last mixes its contribution later on both sides even though actual front/back surfaces swap at the center. Compare right and left views too. renderOrder may improve one region while worsening another or another view. Record view, order, and incorrect regions without calling this a complete solution.

values.variables.0.expected: Occlusion changes, but not every transparency-sorting problem is solved.

values.criteria.1: Explain remaining sorting limitations with screenshots.

values.questions.1: How does not writing depth differ from not testing it?
